description: nf-core/oncoanalyser samplesheet context, aligned to the pinned 3.0.0 schema. Cancer genome and transcriptome analysis of human tumours with the Hartwig WiGiTS tools.

mode.help: Set from the libraries, through the param atlas: wgts for whole-genome DNA and/or whole-transcriptome RNA libraries; targeted only for a panel whose resources are configured (built in only for TSO500, on GRCh37), which no run here has, so configure_run refuses it. Upstream has no default and stops without one. oncoanalyser has no exome mode.

processes_exclude.help: Comma list of WiGiTS components to skip when the researcher's question does not need them, e.g. virusinterpreter (viral integration; its GRIDSS index is another large download), lilac (HLA typing), cuppa (tissue of origin), neo (neoepitopes), orange (the summary report). Upstream's fallback runs every component the data allows.

umi_type.help: Set from the library kit when its reads carry UMIs (Twist, KAPA, MSK-IMPACT or TSO500 UMI adapters), so fastp and REDUX collapse duplicates by UMI. Upstream's fallback is no UMI processing, right for libraries without UMIs.

sequencing_platform.help: Set from the instrument in the D.SEQ metadata: sbx for Roche SBX, ultima for Ultima Genomics. Upstream's fallback is Illumina, which needs nothing set.

pipeline.name: nf-core/oncoanalyser
pipeline.core_rule: Long format, one row per input file: group_id, subject_id, sample_id, sample_type (tumor or normal), sequence_type (dna or rna), filetype, info, filepath. NExtSEEK writes one row per D.SEQ: filetype fastq, both reads in filepath separated by ';', and library_id and lane in info. Paired-end gzipped FASTQ only. The schema also takes BAM, CRAM and earlier WiGiTS outputs; those are not built here.

validation_rules: Write one row per D.SEQ with sample, group_id, sample_type and sequence_type (and subject_id when it differs from group_id). The emitter renames sample to sample_id and writes filetype, info and filepath from the sample's own FASTQ pair; leave those three out.
group_id: one analysis per patient. The UID of the PAT sample in the leaf's lineage; with no PAT, the topmost ancestor's UID. Never invent a shared id to make a pair.

A group holds at most one tumour DNA, one normal DNA and one tumour RNA sample, and always a tumour: tumour-only, tumour with matched normal, and either with tumour RNA are valid; a normal alone is not.

sample_type and sequence_type come from the param atlas verdicts. sample_type is never guessed from a name alone: configure_run shows the user a tumour/normal table for any sample the metadata did not decide.
sample_type here is tumor or normal (the American spelling the schema enums), never the NExtSEEK sample type (D.SEQ).
Single-end samples and samples with no local FASTQ are refused: oncoanalyser aligns paired-end FASTQ only, and an archive download cannot fill a long-format row.
Human only: the run uses the Hartwig GRCh38 bundle (GRCh38_hmf).
notes: The Hartwig reference bundle for GRCh38 (GRCh38_hmf FASTA with its indexes, the BWA-MEM2 index, the GRIDSS index for virus calling, the STAR index for RNA, and the WiGiTS resource files) is not staged on Luria. With no ref_data_* paths set, every run downloads the parts it needs from data.oncoanalyser.com into its Nextflow work folder (tens of GB), which needs outbound HTTPS from the compute node. Staging it once (--mode prepare_reference) and passing the paths is the fix; until then the runtime estimate includes the download.

samplesheet_columns.description: Column-level field dictionary for the nf-core/oncoanalyser input samplesheet (post-alias names).

group_id.description: Groups a patient's samples into one analysis.
group_id.validation_hints: The PAT UID in the lineage; with no PAT, the topmost ancestor's UID.

subject_id.description: Subject or patient id; the same on every row of a group.
subject_id.validation_hints: Left blank, the emitter copies group_id.

sample_id.description: Sample id; output files are named after it.
sample_id.validation_hints: The NExtSEEK D.SEQ UID (the row's `sample`), so results map back to the record.

sample_type.description: Whether the library is from the tumour or the matched normal.
sample_type.validation_hints: From the param atlas verdict; confirmed with the user in configure_run's table when the metadata does not decide it.

sequence_type.validation_hints: From the param atlas verdict. Only tumour samples may be RNA.

filetype.description: The kind of file in filepath.

info.description: For FASTQ: library_id and lane, both required by the pipeline.
info.validation_hints: Written by the emitter: library_id is the sample UID, lane the L00N token of the read-1 name or 001.

filepath.description: Absolute paths of read 1 and read 2, separated by ';'.
filepath.validation_hints: Written by the emitter from the sample's metadata.

report_writer_guidance.purpose: Build an nf-core/oncoanalyser samplesheet from a resolved NExtSEEK D.SEQ cohort of human tumour (and matched normal) libraries.
report_writer_guidance.workflow_role: Selected for a full cancer report: purity and ploidy, somatic SNVs/indels, SVs, copy number, drivers, signatures, HLA, and from tumour RNA, expression and fusions. For general germline or somatic variant calling use sarek.
population_priority: One agent row per D.SEQ: sample (its UID), group_id (the PAT UID), sample_type and sequence_type from the param atlas verdicts.
Where sample_type's verdict is conflict or absent, write your best reading and leave it to the tumour/normal table configure_run shows the user.
Say plainly that each run downloads the Hartwig reference bundle, so the first hours are a download.
final_checks: Every group has a tumour sample, and at most one sample of each kind.

runtime.basis: First guess for one 16-CPU Luria node (Nessie's default submit) on 30-100x WGS; not yet measured on Luria. Refine from real runs.
runtime.setup_label: downloading the Hartwig reference bundle into the work folder (every run repeats it until the bundle is staged on Luria)
